key_insight: The paper shows that the performance gap between homogeneous and heterogeneous asynchronous optimization is fundamentally hard to close, and that several common similarity assumptions are not enough to recover homogeneous-like time complexity.
engineering_relevance: For distributed ML systems, this means weaker data-similarity assumptions may not yield faster asynchronous training, so system design must account for intrinsic heterogeneity limits.
method: Proves impossibility results under widely used first- and second-order similarity assumptions for randomized algorithms.
Tests the interpolation regime and shows weak interpolation alone still does not bridge the gap.
Introduces a minimal assumption pair—strong interpolation plus local Polyak-Lojasiewicz—to obtain a sharper time bound.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical analysis and proof-based time-complexity bounds, with no empirical experiments mentioned.
watch_item: The improved bound depends on stronger structural assumptions, so it may not apply to many practical nonconvex or highly non-identical training workloads.
paper_title: Bridging the Gap Between Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Asynchronous Optimization Is Surprisingly Difficult
